types.name: Company
types.description:
Represents a single company in the system.
Historically it could be any type of company, but over time each company type has been implemented as its own model.
Now Company is mostly a Subcontractor, which is our primary focus.
Note that for historical reasons, architects/owners/bond providers are still represented as Companies.

types.name: ContractLienRightsMilestone
types.description:
A milestone in the lien rights lifecycle that will be required for this contract
based on its state's lien rights requirements. The milestone may already be completed,
or may have a known or unknown deadline in the future.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name of the document required. Customizable only for some milestone types.

fields.name: deadlineInterval
fields.description:
A description of the canonical deadline, in reference to an anchor date. A deadline
should exist for all milestones except of type PRELIMINARY_NOTICE_CONTINGENT_NOTICE_FILED
and OWNER_NOTICE_FILED, which are included only if they are completed milestones.

fields.name: lateDeadlineInterval
fields.description:
If late filing is allowed, this is the amount of time relative to filing that the filer is protected.
 Late filing only applies to preliminary notice deadlines.

fields.name: possibleDeadlineExceptions
fields.description:
Any shortened deadlines due to owner notice that may affect this deadline. This will be the complete
list based on state requirements, regardless of whether any notices have actually been filed.

fields.name: requirementType
fields.description:
The requirement type for this milestone. Note that this is only a reflection of the canonical state law for
this milestone, NOT whether or not this specific milestone is required based on project status or aging pay apps.

fields.name: contingentOnNotice
fields.description:
If this deadline is contingent on the filing of another notice (e.g. for prelims), this is
the name of that notice. (If it has been filed, there will be a completed milestone provided
under `completedByMilestone`.)

fields.name: payApp
fields.description: If the milestone is a monthly pre-lien, it is based on either a pay app or pre-siteline pay app

fields.name: contractDeadline
fields.description:
The actual deadline for this contract, if known based on key dates. This is calculated based
on the deadline interval, granularity, modifier, and anchor, where the anchor corresponds to
a completed key date. There may be an exception if a notice was filed and the deadline was
adjusted based on a `LienDeadlineNoticeRequirementNewDeadline`.

fields.name: affectedByMilestone
fields.description:
If this milestone is dependent on other milestones, for example:
- A notice of commencement filing milestone, if this is a preliminary notice contingent on that notice
- An owner notice filing milestone, if this is a pre-lien, lien, or enforcement deadline that is shortened
  by the filing of that notice

fields.name: completedByMilestone
fields.description: If the milestone has already been completed, this is a reference to the completed milestone

fields.name: additionalNotes
fields.description: Additional context or details on this milestone's requirements

fields.name: metadata
fields.description: If the milestone has metadata, this is a reference to the metadata - for example, generated forms

types.name: PayAppRequirementGroup
types.description:
Pay-apps determine which requirements to show by iterating over each requirement group and picking
one requirement from the group. Requirements are selected by picking the first one in their group
which meets all its conditions. It is possible that a requirement group has no eligible requirement
to show, in which case the group is ignored altogether.
Group order is determined by `PayAppRequirementGroup.order`.
Example:
- Group (order = 1)
  - Requirement (groupOrder = 1)
  - Requirement (groupOrder = 2)
- Group (order = 2)
  - Requirement (groupOrder = 1)
  - Requirement (groupOrder = 2)
  - Requirement (groupOrder = 3)

The subcontractor, GC, or owner that created the original form. For example, the AGA G702's

The GC that created the original form (if any).

fields.name: totalRetention

fields.name: changeOrderRequests

 total value changes in a pay app, use the pay app start as the approved date.

types.name: PayApp

Billing type extracted from the contract billing type when pay app is created.

fields.name: uploadedFile
fields.description: If provided, we'll use this file instead of generating it on the fly

fields.name: finalInvoice
fields.description:
Generated when the pay app is signed so any future submissions and downloads include the exact
invoice that was signed. This file includes only the "invoice" forms, i.e. pay app requirements
and primary lien waiver. Other attachments will still be re-generated.

fields.name: progress
fields.description:
A list of progress values for their respective SOV line items.
Not used for QUICK pay apps.
This array is empty for all other types of pay apps.

fields.name: amountLineItems
fields.description:
A list of amount line items for the pay app.
Only used for QUICK pay apps.
This array is empty for all other types of pay apps.

fields.name: rateTableItems
fields.description: Only for T&M

fields.name: rateTableFees
fields.description:
Only for T&M.
Warning: this includes *all* fees, including group fees.

fields.name: rateTableGroups
fields.description: Only for T&M

fields.description:
Link back to rate table that was used to create a T&M pay app.
It will always exist for T&M pay apps, although it might be archived.
Always null for pay apps that are not T&M.

fields.name: haveContractFeesChanged
fields.description: Whether fees have changed on the contract since the pay app was created

fields.name: haveContractTaxesChanged
fields.description: Whether the taxes have changed on the contract since the pay app was created

fields.name: hasContractRateTableChanged
fields.description: Whether the contract rate table was swapped or updated since the pay app was created

fields.name: draftSubmittedAt
fields.description:
This is the time at which a pay app draft was submitted. It is cleared when a pay app is edited
and won't ever be set if the pay app was never submitted while it was a draft.

fields.name: sentToSignerAt
fields.description: This is the time at which a pay app was first sent to signer for review/signature.

fields.name: lastSubmitted
fields.description:
Returns the most recent status log from a submission or sync, even if the pay app is in DRAFT.
We return the entire log, rather than just the date, so the client can tell
whether the latest submit event was a submission or a sync.

fields.name: retentionOnly
fields.description: Used to determine whether the type of pay app is 'normal' or 'retention-only'.

fields.name: billingStart

Start date of the billing period for this pay app. Usually start of the month.
Note that it's a point in time and that you'll need the project timezone to determine the month.

fields.name: billingEnd
fields.description:
End date of the billing period for this pay app. Usually end of the month.
Note that it's a point in time and that you'll need the project timezone to determine the month.
We use this field to determine the "month" of the pay app.

fields.name: description
fields.description:
Description of the pay app.
Eg: "Pay App #1 (January)"

fields.name: internalDueDate
fields.description:
Date before which invoice must be submitted by the sub project manager to the sub accountant
(internal deadline).

fields.name: payAppDueDate
fields.description: Date before which the entire PayApp must be submitted to the GC (external deadline).

fields.name: currentBilled
fields.description:

materials.

fields.name: currentRetention
fields.description: This is the current retention for this PayApp.

fields.name: amountDuePreTax
fields.description: Current billed - retention held + retention released. This is pre-tax.

fields.name: amountDuePostTax
fields.description: Amount due, post tax. This is amountDuePreTax + amountDueTaxAmount

fields.name: totalRetention
fields.description: This is the total retention held for this PayApp including the current period.

fields.name: invoiceReady
fields.description: A single bit to describe if an invoice has been marked as completed by a sub project manager.

fields.name: attachments
fields.description: List of attachments to include as backup in the pay app

fields.name: legalDocuments
fields.description: List of legal documents to include as backup in the pay app

fields.name: lienWaivers
fields.description: List of LienWaivers for the top-tier sub and all lower-tier subs

fields.name: emailedContacts

Array of CompanyContact references that were emailed a PDF version of this PayApp. This is only
used when the general contractor is not using Siteline to administer PayApps.

fields.name: ccContacts
fields.description: List of CompanyContact references that were CC'd on the email version of this PayApp.

fields.name: lastSync
fields.description: The last write sync for this entity, completed or not

fields.name: lastSyncIfSuccessful
fields.description: The last write sync for this entity. Null if not successful

fields.name: lastErpSyncs
fields.description:
The last ERP syncs for this entity, successful or not.

per Siteline contract, this can have as many syncs as there are ERP contracts.
These must be stored in the database because they need to reset when editing the invoice.

fields.name: texturaRejectedAt
fields.description: If an invoice was rejected by the GC in Textura, this is the date it was rejected

fields.name: texturaRejectionReason
fields.description:
If an invoice was rejected by the GC in Textura, this is the reason it was rejected for.
Note that this might not always be provided in the textura message that we parse, so it can be null
while texturaRejectedAt is set. Do not rely on this field to determine whether an invoice was rejected.

fields.name: physicalSignatureRequired

fields.name: payAppNumber
fields.description: Computes the pay app's number

fields.name: invoiceNumber
fields.description: Optional invoice number for this pay app, to be used with template variables, if it exists.

fields.name: retentionInvoiceNumber

Optional invoice number for retention release invoices synced to ERPs,
when retention release is separate from the normal invoice.

Templates that are pinned to this pay-app. Since @oneToMany cannot be nullable, formTemplates can
only be an array with 0 or more elements. This is why we use a flag to determine whether to get
templates from the array, or from the contract that this pay-app belongs to.

fields.name: comments

that was used to mark it paid. Otherwise returns null.

on what the end user recorded. If the pay app has not been paid, then this returns null/undefined.

fields.name: isBalanceManuallyClosed

mark the pay app balance as closed so the remaining amount isn't considered due and doesn't appear
in aging reports.

fields.name: previousRetentionBilled

fields.name: currentProgressAndRetentionBilled

fields.name: statusLogs

fields.name: userFacingStatus

Human-readable status of the pay app.

fields.name: balanceToFinish
fields.description: Total balance left to finish after this pay app.

fields.name: automaticallyReadBilling

enumValues.name: WEEKLY_PAY_APP
enumValues.description:
Weekly emails sent to all users have three types of errors: pay app, legal requirement, or lien rights.
Each of these sets can be configured to be turned off. If all are turned off, the
weekly email will not be sent.
Note that the weekly external is specific to PMs, who have an internal deadline and might
not be concerned with external deadlines. They likely only want to know if the internal
deadline was hit. The weekly pay app email will surface internal deadlines to PMs and
external deadlines to accountants (this is determined by the user's billing deadline).
Notification of type WEEKLY_PAY_APP_EXTERNAL_PM does not apply to users with external
deadlines.

enumValues.name: DAILY_PAY_APP

Daily emails sent to all users have three types of errors: pay app, legal requirement, or lien rights.
Each of these sets can be configured to be turned off. If all are turned off, the
daily email will not be sent.
Note that the daily external is specific to PMs, who have an internal deadline and might
not be concerned with external deadlines. They likely only want to know if the internal
deadline was hit. The daily pay app email will surface internal deadlines to PMs and
external deadlines to accountants (this is determined by the user's billing deadline).
Notification of type WEEKLY_PAY_APP_EXTERNAL_PM does not apply to users with external
deadlines.

enumValues.name: MERGE_ORIGINAL_LINE_ITEMS
enumValues.description:
The default method of importing change orders is to match change orders to SOV line items,
use the revised amount as the line item amount, and mark the corresponding line item as a
change order (regardless of whether it had an original amount prior to the change order). This
affects ERP integrations only.

enumValues.name: CREATE_NEW_LINE_ITEMS
enumValues.description:
In special cases, customers may prefer for change orders in their ERP to be imported as
new, individual line items on the SOV, rather than being merged into their linked line item.
This means the SOV we read from the ERP may *not* match the SOV in the ERP. This logic will
be used only when reading the SOV to import into Siteline, not when allocating invoice billing.

enumValues.name: SINGLE_PROJECT_FLAT_SOV
enumValues.description:
The default method is to import a single project with the contract SOV in Siteline, with no extra
handling for combo jobs. The line items are imported directly, with no special grouping.

enumValues.name: SINGLE_PROJECT_GROUPED_SOV

group the contract line items by job if there are multiple jobs linked by the line items

enumValues.name: MULTIPLE_PROJECTS
enumValues.description:
In this method, we will import each job as a separate project, and the corresponding SOVs will
include only the subset of the integration contract line items that link to that job. There will
be no special grouping of the SOV line items.

enumValues.name: WEEKLY
enumValues.description:
Recurs weekly starting on the startDate that is specified on the LegalRequirement. i.e. if it
is weekly starting Tuesday, 9/14/2021, then it recurs weekly on Tuesdays starting 9/14.

enumValues.name: MONTHLY
enumValues.description:
Recurs monthly starting on the startDate that is specified on the LegalRequirement.
Note: we don't allow the 29th, 30th, or 31st because those dates don't make sense in February.

enumValues.name: QUARTERLY
enumValues.description:
Recurs every 3 months starting on the startDate that is specified on the LegalRequirement.
Note: we don't allow the 29th, 30th, or 31st because those dates don't make sense in February.

enumValues.name: YEARLY
enumValues.description: Recurs yearly on the startDate that is specified on the LegalRequirement.

enumValues.name: END_OF_MONTH
enumValues.description: Recurs monthly on the last day of the month. i.e. 1/31, 2/28 (or 2/29), 3/31, 4/30, etc.

enumValues.name: USER_INPUT
enumValues.description:
Does not recur on any specific frequency. The user inputs the expiration date every time they
upload a document and it doesn't prompt you for a new document till the previous one expires.

enumValues.name: NEVER
enumValues.description:
These requirements will never expire. Only one document ever has to be uploaded and no expiration
date is associated with it.

enumValues.name: NONE
enumValues.description:
There is no retention tracking.
This only applies to QUICK projects.

enumValues.name: PROJECT
enumValues.description:
Retention is tracked at the project level. This means that a fixed percent of the total billed on
the project is held. For example, if a subcontractor has billed for $100,000 on the project so far
and their PayApp retentionPercent is set to 10%, then the GC has $10,000 retention held.

enumValues.name: PAY_APP
enumValues.description:
Retention is tracked at the pay app level. This means that a fixed percent of the total billed on
that pay app is held and added to the fixed amount of each past pay app. For example, if a
subcontractor has billed for $10,000 last pay app with 10% rate and $10,000 this pay app with 5%
rate, then the GC has $1,500 retention held.

enumValues.name: STANDARD
enumValues.description:
Retention is tracked on the sov line item progress level. This means that a fixed percent of the
total billed on a line item progress is held and added up. For example, lets say a subcontractor
has $10,000 billed from past months and an additional $10,000 in current progress billing. If
their progressRetentionPercent in the past pay apps is 10%, but it is set to 5% on this pay app,
then the GC has $1,500 retention held.

enumValues.name: LINE_ITEM
enumValues.description:
Retention is tracked on the sov line item level. This means that a fixed percent of the total
billed on a line item is held and added up. For example, lets say a subcontractor has $10,000
billed from past months and an additional $10,000 in current progress billing. If their
progressRetentionPercent is 10%, then the GC has $2,000 retention held.

enumValues.name: NONE
enumValues.description: Tax is not calculated at all

enumValues.name: SINGLE_TAX_GROUP
enumValues.description:
All line items have the same tax group.
If a tax group other than `defaultTaxGroup` is assigned, we throw an error.

enumValues.name: MULTIPLE_TAX_GROUPS
enumValues.description: Line items can have different tax groups, as long they belong to the company.

enumValues.name: TAX_DISTRICT
enumValues.description:
Set a tax district on the invoice so that Sage calculates taxes automatically.
Taxes will appear on the AR invoice in the Sales tax field.
There will be only one line item containing the pre-tax amount of the pay app.
All payments (pre-tax + taxes) will go to the specified income account.

enumValues.name: SITELINE_SOV_POST_TAX
enumValues.description:
Some customers like Guthrie need to explicitly record taxes in the SOV, as separate line items
which are billed for month over month.
For instance the SOV would have:
 1. NON-TAXABLE LABOR
 2. TAXABLE LABOR
 3. TAX ON LABOR

In this case, the tax amount is the billing value of "TAX ON LABOR", and the Siteline SOV is
considered to be post tax. Siteline tax calculation is disabled on these contracts.
Tax amount on the AR invoice will come from these individual items, which must be passed in
at sync time via the `taxLineItemIds` payload field.

The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByURL`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

directives.name: new
directives.description:
Indicates that an argument or input field is new.
If the field is optional, it will be optional both on the backend and frontend.
If the field is required, it will be required on the frontend, but optional on the backend to maintain
backwards compatibility.

To add a new backward compatible field, follow these steps:
 - Add the field to the schema with the @new directive. Make the field required. Backend will accept
   null values but frontend will not.

   resolver(field: String! @new): Response!

 - After the frontend is fully updated, make the field optional so that old clients can still send
   requests without the field.

   resolver(field: String @new): Response!

 - Deploy the change.
 - A week or two after deploying the new field, make the field required, remove the @new directive,
   and update the Joi schemas to make the field required.

   resolver(field: String!): Response!
